proposals.title: A multiphase, common-denominator census of AGN-driven outflows
proposals.hypothesis: The inferred frequency and impact of AGN outflows depend strongly on gas phase, and a common-denominator multiphase census will change which feedback conclusions are supportable.

prior_evidence.statement: High-redshift quasar molecular-gas work provides one tracer of AGN impact on cold reservoirs, but it cannot represent all gas phases.

links.label: molecular gas reservoirs in quasars
links.title: AGN feedback on molecular gas reservoirs in quasars at z~2.4

prior_evidence.statement: Young radio-galaxy outflow studies provide a complementary radio/ionized-gas efficiency perspective.

links.label: young radio-galaxy outflows
links.title: AGN-driven outflows and feedback efficiency in young radio galaxies

prior_evidence.statement: The local evidence summary includes AGN/outflow debate anchors that should be treated as provenance, not as a complete population denominator.

proposals.remaining_uncertainty: Different tracers select different temperature/density phases and apertures, so current outflow rates may not be comparable or population-representative.
proposals.data_plan: Parent AGN sample selected before outflow detection; MUSE/MaNGA ionized gas, ALMA CO molecular gas, HI/Na D or UV absorption for neutral gas, and JWST/NIRSpec at higher redshift; matched inactive controls.
proposals.decision_criterion: Recompute outflow occurrence, mass-loading, and kinetic power under a common selection denominator and aperture model. The claim that AGN outflows are common or important is supportable only for phases and mass/redshift ranges where tracer-corrected occurrence remains high.
proposals.limitations: Mass conversion factors differ by phase; avoid combining phase-specific mass outflow rates without explicit conversion uncertainties.

proposals.title: Distinguishing molecular-gas depletion from suppressed star-formation efficiency in quenched galaxies
proposals.hypothesis: In quenched or transitioning galaxies, low star formation is driven primarily by reduced molecular-gas fraction in some regimes and by reduced star-formation efficiency in others.

prior_evidence.statement: The local evidence summary separates reservoir-response questions from AGN mechanism claims, motivating a direct gas-fraction versus efficiency test.
Molecular-gas reservoir observations in quasars show that AGN can coincide with disturbed cold gas, but they do not alone distinguish depletion from suppressed efficiency.

links.label: quasar molecular-gas reservoir evidence
links.title: AGN feedback on molecular gas reservoirs in quasars at z~2.4

prior_evidence.statement: Environment/AGN comparisons against SDSS motivate separating gas supply, environment, and internal feedback rather than treating quenching as one scalar outcome.

links.label: environment and AGN quenching versus SDSS
links.title: Environment and AGN feedback in quenching local galaxies: simulations versus SDSS

proposals.remaining_uncertainty: A quenched galaxy can have little gas or inefficient star formation in the gas it retains; those mechanisms imply different feedback and replenishment physics.
proposals.data_plan: ALMA CO for molecular gas mass, dust continuum as a cross-check, Hα/UV/IR SFR indicators, optical morphology and stellar population ages, environment labels, and matched star-forming/transition/quiescent controls.
proposals.decision_criterion: Decompose sSFR offsets into gas-fraction and depletion-time terms at fixed mass, redshift, and environment. Reservoir depletion is supported when gas fraction drives the offset; efficiency suppression is supported when depletion time changes dominate with gas retained.
proposals.limitations: CO-to-H2 conversion, aperture mismatch, and SFR timescale indicators must be propagated into the decision criterion.

proposals.title: Forward-modelled validation of cosmological feedback prescriptions
proposals.hypothesis: If subgrid feedback prescriptions are correct, forward-modelled mock observations from simulations should reproduce observed gas fractions, quenched fractions, outflow tracers, and morphology distributions under the same selection functions.

prior_evidence.statement: IllustrisTNG quenched-fraction analyses explicitly tie quenching outcomes to AGN feedback, environment, and preprocessing in simulations.

links.label: IllustrisTNG quenched fractions
links.title: Quenched fractions in the IllustrisTNG simulations

prior_evidence.statement: Horizon-AGN links AGN feedback to morphological diversity, making morphology a testable output rather than background context.

links.label: Horizon-AGN morphology and AGN feedback
links.title: The Horizon-AGN simulation: morphological diversity promoted by AGN feedback

prior_evidence.statement: Hydrodynamic quenching simulations motivate observationally matched validation, not direct import of simulation conclusions.

links.label: AGN-driven quenching simulation implications
links.title: AGN-driven quenching of star formation: morphological and dynamical implications

proposals.remaining_uncertainty: Simulations are often compared to derived quantities rather than to observables passed through the same survey selection, aperture, and sensitivity functions.
proposals.data_plan: IllustrisTNG/Horizon-AGN/EAGLE-like public simulation outputs; synthetic MaNGA/MUSE/ALMA/X-ray/radio observables; real comparison samples from SDSS/MaNGA, ALMA follow-up, and group catalogues.
proposals.decision_criterion: Generate survey-matched mocks and compare joint distributions of gas fraction, quenched fraction, morphology, outflow incidence, and halo environment. A feedback model is constrained when residuals exceed observational uncertainties in a physically coherent subset of observables.
proposals.limitations: Different subgrid models can produce degenerate macroscopic observables; results should report which observables discriminate rather than ranking simulations globally.

title: Galaxy Evolution — Research proposals on feedback tracers and model validation
reader_facing_summary: This page presents three proposal-style research programmes on multiphase outflows, molecular-gas depletion versus efficiency, and forward-modelled simulation validation. Duplicate themes are consolidated so each proposal targets a distinct physical uncertainty.
